notes: No introduction, methods or tables in the packet: HYP/DES/PRC nodes are text with requires_unseen. Spine shape: one surface-chemistry line (n6 -> m1, n7 -> m2), one surface-structure line that compares the two orientations inside itself (n9/n10 for (110) contrasted with n11/n12 and m3/n15 for (320)), and one bulk control branch (n13/n14, TEM) that answers the decomposition hypothesis n2 and is linked to the surface line by contrasts. Grain-boundary chemistry (n8) is kept off the spine: it serves only to show that the Ni/Mn co-segregation is a surface and not a grain-boundary effect. Audit: a1 (EDS bulk Mn depletion at the boundary) contradicts the SAM surface Mn enrichment of F2b; the paper states both and never reconciles them. d2 records the irreversible Mn loss above 873 K, d3 the XPS/EDS composition disagreement. Figure readings that fall short of the text: F4a arrow vectors give |b*|/|a*| ~ 2 and ~ 78-80 deg against the quoted 1.9 and 74 +/- 1 deg (o17 partial); the F4b histogram peak train is regular but 0.5 and 1.0 A cannot be separated by eye (o19 partial); the F6b EELS maps are noise-dominated (o24 partial); the 7.2 A doubled periodicity of F3f is not measurable at that scale (o15 partial). Lost by design: supplementary figures S1-S5 (sputtering test, Cr/Co grain-boundary maps, no Ni segregation, expected (110) structure) are referenced in the text but absent from the packet, and the EDS line profile of F5 is text-only. Judge r07: n12 was split into n12 (terrace-and-step morphology, 0.5/1.0 A steps, produced by n5 and premised on k1) and n15 (the ~6.5 A row corrugation on the terraces, explained by m3 and evidenced by o20), because the two halves have different evidence and different explanations. n7 lost its memory-effect clause, which d2 already states.

split_nodes.why: the label stated two claims about the (320) surface with different evidence and different causes: the terrace-and-step morphology with 0.5 and 1.0 A steps (o18, o19; step heights follow from d(320) and d(320)/2, i.e. the k1 premise) and the ~6.5 A row corrugation on the terraces (o20; caused by the two-(110)-plus-one-(100) facet succession, i.e. m3 with the k2 model). m3 -explains-> n12 previously explained only half of the node it pointed at, and n12 -causes-> p2 uses only the other half (the (320) surface is the flat one).

merged_nodes.why: 'later preparations stay Mn-poor' duplicated d2 ('Once annealed above 873 K for more than an hour, later preparations stay Mn-poor for several cycles'). d2 is the node that carries the evidence for it (o3, the two open Mn squares) and the qualifies edge into n6, while the o2 evidence on n7 reads only the collapse. n7 keeps the collapse claim, d2 keeps the memory effect.

F2a/F5a/F5b list only instrument banners under annotations; the '(320)'/'(110)' grain labels appear as tokens but the nodes read the boundary, the striations and the map contrast, not the labels. F4a's '80eV' and F4b's '[001]' are panel identity and an orientation marker, not the reading.
